Domain Expectations: MediaMetadata validates non-negative durations; zero-duration media is allowed but cannot advance playback
Player play() sets state to Playing only when a current media exists; pause() sets Paused; stop() sets Stopped and resets position to 0
Player seek(ms) clamps to [0, current_media_duration] and preserves state (Playing/Paused) while resetting last-tick reference

Player update_to_now() uses IClock to compute elapsed time since last tick when in Playing; advances position and clamps to duration; on reaching duration, sets state to Paused and position to duration
Player supports set_volume(int 0..100) and mute/unmute; volume clamped to bounds; mute is independent from volume level
Playlist supports add(), size(), get(index), select(index) returning bool, current_index(), next()/prev() with bounds; no wrap-around by default
Switching playlist item resets player position to 0 and sets state to Stopped; subsequent play() begins from 0
MonotonicClock reads steady time; ManualClock provides deterministic control for tests and demos
Domain Reasoning: Playback timing is a pure-domain responsibility driven by a clock boundary; implement IClock with ManualClock (deterministic) and MonotonicClock (real-time) to separate environment from logic
Player manages state transitions: Stopped, Paused, Playing; updates position using clock deltas, clamping to media duration
Playlist provides deterministic navigation and selection among MediaMetadata entries; navigation returns success/failure without side effects beyond selection
MediaMetadata contains validated duration and descriptive fields; duration bounds checks are critical for seek and playback clamping
Volume and mute are domain properties: volume as an integer 0–100, independent mute flag; effective output can be inferred but no audio output
Seeking must clamp within [0, duration] and update last-timestamp references coherently
Runtime/App composes the clock, playlist, and player for a small deterministic demo without I/O loops or GUI
Tests must drive ManualClock to assert deterministic playback progress and rule enforcement

Product Goals: Deliver a clean, deterministic C++17 core for a headless video player domain (no decoding) with clear separation of concerns
Provide a minimal, strictly specified build and test pipeline that is self-contained and reproducible
Ensure strong API contracts and input validation to simplify future extension and UI integration
Requirement Analysis: We must produce a C++17 repository with strict protocol: CMakeLists.txt as the sole build file, src/Main.cpp as the minimal runtime entry returning Runtime::App().run_demo(), and tests/test_main.cpp as the only test file with a single int main(). The architecture must use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. Deterministic time must be provided via an IClock boundary with a ManualClock for tests and a MonotonicClock for runtime. The 64-bit timing contract is strict: every header that names a signed 64-bit integer directly includes <cstdint> and uses std::int64_t spelling; IClock.h must begin with <cstdint> and declare virtual std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept = 0; ManualClock and MonotonicClock must override exactly that signature consistently in headers and sources. Domain behavior includes media metadata (duration), playlist navigation without wrap, playback state transitions (play/pause/stop), seek and duration clamping, volume and mute handling, and a headless deterministic update path. Tests need to be concise (2–4 tests, under ~150 LOC), deterministic, and headless. The CMake test target must be built directly (no find_package), registered with add_test, and invoked via ctest. Public API must be canonical so tests import only headers. Files should be small (ideally under 150 LOC each) and ordered by dependency to avoid circular includes.
Requirement Pool: Preserve protocol-required files and paths exactly (CMakeLists.txt; src/Main.cpp; tests/test_main.cpp) and build via ctest
Enforce fixed 64-bit time type rules and exact IClock signature across headers/sources
Implement core domain behaviors: metadata, playlist navigation, playback states, seek clamping, volume/mute
Provide ManualClock and MonotonicClock with deterministic and monotonic behavior respectively
Deliver concise deterministic tests (2–4) covering runtime wiring and key rules
Testing Constraints: Exactly one protocol-level test file: tests/test_main.cpp
No third-party frameworks; a single self-contained int main() using only the C++17 standard library
Deterministic, headless tests; no GUI, no I/O loops, no randomness, no network
Tests include only headers from include/, never src/*.cpp
Cover runtime wiring (Runtime::App) and at least one core rule (e.g., deterministic playback advancement)
UI / UX / Interaction Design draft: Headless runtime with a tiny demo: construct a playlist, create a Player with ManualClock, perform a simple sequence (play, advance time, pause/stop), and exit. No GUI rendering or input loops. Tests avoid real rendering and manual input by using ManualClock and direct API calls.
User Stories: As a user, I can load a playlist of media items and move to next/previous items deterministically
As a user, I can play, pause, and stop playback and see position bounded by each media’s duration
As a user, I can seek to a specific position within media and the player clamps to valid bounds
As a user, I can set volume and toggle mute independently of volume level
As a developer, I can run a deterministic demo and tests without external dependencies or manual steps
